body.objective: Decide whether the phase of the complex compensator is a healthy relational clock and supports a genuinely relational causal redshift observable in the same compensator-extended action that generates the invariant metric.
body.stop_condition: Import the terminal classical complex-compensator BV parent, reduced pairing, causal homotopies, D action and internal-phase action by exact hashes. Construct a nontrivial phase-gradient clock solution with all background equations, regularity and charge conditions satisfied. Compute the covariant phase-space generators of raw D, phase rotations and every required combined Berger-type generator on the unrestricted and selected charge fibres. Build emitter, receiver, transported phase and detector records from the same action, then construct O_A(theta=tau_clock) and a two-event frequency-shift observable using g_hat rather than a coordinate-frequency ratio. Prove gauge invariance, causal support, clock monotonicity on the declared patch, reduced-pairing health and exact agreement or deviation from the Einstein redshift in the low-curvature phase. Determine whether total D remains degenerate, becomes charged, or is replaced by a combined generator. If any same-action apparatus row is absent, land the first exact missing representation and do not promote the observable.
body.current_gate: healthy phase-clock reduction plus one same-action relational redshift theorem
body.forbid: no radial compensator called a physical clock after it is contracted as gauge; no prescribed external clock, rod, emitter or detector called relational; no coordinate frequency ratio called redshift; no raw-D/K or D-plus-phase generator identification; no positivity inferred before quotienting; no import from the old Berger action without an explicit action morphism; no phenomenology, particle, scattering or quantum promotion

a charge theorem deciding which time generator is gauge
